assignments.brief_reason: Uses incitement-to-violence as the removal threshold while permitting broader speech.
Disallows slurs/bad/off-putting content as toxic speech, consistent with removing toxicity.
Rejects profanity/intense mockery while allowing respectful disagreement, aligning with removing toxicity.
Focuses on reasoning soundness and penalizing anger rather than threat/toxicity criteria in the codebook.
Relies on severity/tone and framing; fits removal for hostile/toxic/inflammatory language more than violence exceptions.
Affect and perceived truthfulness drive passing decisions; not clearly threat/toxicity or violence-specific.
Emphasizes fair/respectful/constructive dialogue and avoiding division, closer to consistent equitable judging than violence/toxicity-only thresholds.
Removes mostly for vitriol/hostility and expects facts over hostile opinions.
Treats profanity/vulgar language as an automatic disqualifier due to animosity/arguments (toxicity).
Filters offensive language and directed targeting; primarily a toxicity/offensiveness removal rationale.
Swearing alone is tolerated, but attacks on people are not—matches removing threats/toxicity.
Uses rationality vs name-calling to judge potential devolution; not directly captured by the provided themes.
Credits the mirror-pair with enforcing consistent attention to tone/substance across viewpoints.
Distinguishes true conversation from ad hominem attacks; aligns with removing toxic/hostile content.
Uses profanity as a hard gating rule; aligns with removing toxicity.
Mentions baseline partisan inclination as affecting judgment; not a specific moderation threshold.
Explicitly aims for neutral/equitable evaluation across the pair, applying the same standard to both sides.
Concerns redundancy/needlessness of pairs, which is outside the toxicity/violence/equitable-standard themes.
Default allow with removal triggers for inciting violence or attacking a person/group.
Uses a general harm/harmlessness criterion, which is not explicitly mapped to the codebook's violence/toxicity themes.
